docs.intro: Welcome. This help explains how calculator logic works in **blocks**, in **formula code**, and in the **full script** — all three edit the same underlying formula tree.

plus.title: Addition (+)
plus.blockUsage: Drag the **+** operator between two blocks in the formula workspace.
plus.codeUsage: Write `a + b` with field references, e.g. `field_item.qty + 1`.

minus.title: Subtraction (−)
minus.description: Subtracts the right value from the left.
minus.blockUsage: Drag **−** between blocks, e.g. revenue minus cost.

multiply.title: Multiplication (×)
multiply.codeUsage: Write `a * b` — the usual qty × price pattern.

divide.title: Division (÷)
divide.description: Divides the left value by the right. Division by zero shows a warning and returns 0.
divide.codeUsage: Write `a / b`. Parentheses group sub-expressions: `(a + b) / c`.

gt.title: Greater than (>)
gt.description: Returns 1 when the left value is greater than the right, otherwise 0.
gt.blockUsage: Use in code or drag **>** between blocks, e.g. for IF conditions.

lt.title: Less than (<)
lt.description: Returns 1 when the left value is smaller than the right, otherwise 0.
lt.blockUsage: Use in code or drag **<** between blocks.
lt.codeUsage: Use `a < b` inside `IF` or compare calc outputs.

gte.title: Greater or equal (≥)
gte.description: Returns 1 when the left value is greater than or equal to the right, otherwise 0.
gte.blockUsage: Type **>=** in code or drag **≥** from the palette.
gte.codeUsage: Type `>=` in code (not a single Unicode char).

lte.title: Less or equal (≤)
lte.description: Returns 1 when the left value is less than or equal to the right, otherwise 0.
lte.blockUsage: Type **<=** in code or drag **≤** from the palette.

eq.title: Equal (==)
eq.description: Returns 1 when both values are equal, otherwise 0.
eq.blockUsage: Type **==** in code or drag **=** from the palette.

neq.title: Not equal (≠)
neq.blockUsage: Type **!=** in code or drag **≠** from the palette.

sum.title: SUM
sum.blockUsage: Drag **SUM** from the palette and fill the inner slots with values to add.
sum.codeUsage: `SUM(a, b, c)` — comma-separated; nest calls: `SUM(a, SUM(b, c))`.

count.title: COUNT
count.blockUsage: Drag **COUNT** and add values inside the brackets.
count.codeUsage: `COUNT(a, b, …)` counts how many arguments you pass.

avg.title: AVG
avg.blockUsage: Drag **AVG** from aggregates in the palette.

sum-rows.title: SUM_ROWS
sum-rows.description: Sum of an expression evaluated for each row in a line-items table.
sum-rows.blockUsage: Under a line-items field, drag **SUM rows** and build the per-row formula inside.
sum-rows.codeUsage: `SUM_ROWS(field_lines, row.qty * row.var_cost)` — `row.*` only inside the second argument.

count-rows.title: COUNT_ROWS
count-rows.description: Number of rows in a line-items table (same expression evaluated per row for consistency).
count-rows.blockUsage: Use **COUNT rows** from the line-items group in the palette.

avg-rows.title: AVG_ROWS
avg-rows.description: Average of an expression over all rows in a line-items table.
avg-rows.blockUsage: Drag **AVG rows** for a table field.

min-rows.title: MIN_ROWS
min-rows.description: Minimum of an expression across table rows.

max-rows.title: MAX_ROWS
max-rows.description: Maximum of an expression across table rows.

if.title: IF
if.description: Picks the second value when the condition is non-zero, otherwise the third.
if.blockUsage: Drag **IF** and fill condition, then-branch, and else-branch.
if.codeUsage: `IF(condition, thenValue, elseValue)` — condition true when ≠ 0. Example: `IF(field_item.qty >= 10, price * 0.9, price)`.

round.title: ROUND
round.description: Rounds a numeric value to the given number of decimal places (0–10).
round.blockUsage: Drag **ROUND** and fill value and optional decimals.

quantity.title: Quantity (.qty)
quantity.description: User-entered quantity for an input field.
quantity.blockUsage: Drag the field's quantity chip from the palette.

property.title: Property (.var_*)
property.description: A numeric property on an input (cost, price, etc.).
property.blockUsage: Drag a property block under its field group.
property.codeUsage: Reference as `field_item.var_cost` (property id after the dot).

constant.title: Constant
constant.description: Fixed value defined in calculator constants.
constant.blockUsage: Drag a constant from the palette into the formula.

macro.title: Macro
macro.description: Reusable formula fragment defined in calculator macros.
macro.blockUsage: Drag a macro chip into any formula.
macro.codeUsage: Use macro id alone: `macro_sheet_cost` (defined in macros.calc).

calculation.title: Calculation
calculation.blockUsage: Drag a calculation reference when building outputs or other calcs.
calculation.codeUsage: Use calc id: `calc_subtotal` (must be declared above in dependency order).

row-property.title: Row property (row.*)
row-property.description: Property of the current row inside SUM_ROWS / line-items formulas.
row-property.blockUsage: Inside a row aggregate bracket, use row property blocks.

input.title: input
input.description: Declares an input field with properties and optional quantity.
input.codeUsage: Declare fields the user fills. Properties become `field_id.var_*`.
input.blockUsage: Add inputs in the builder sidebar; they appear in the block palette under each field.

constant.title: constant
constant.description: Fixed numeric constant used in formulas.
constant.codeUsage: Fixed value; reference as `const_id` in formulas.

calc.title: calc
calc.description: Intermediate calculation with a formula block.
calc.blockUsage: Calculation fields section → open formula → blocks or code.

output.title: output
output.description: Final result shown to the user.
output.codeUsage: Shown after Calculate; use a `formula { return … }` block in the output declaration.
output.blockUsage: Result fields section → formula defines what the user sees.

macro.title: macro
macro.description: Reusable formula fragment; referenced by id in other formulas.
macro.codeUsage: Declare once in `macros.calc`, use as `macro_sheet_cost` elsewhere.
macro.blockUsage: Define the macro body with blocks in the Macros section; drag the macro chip into any formula.

docs.introShort: Reference cards for every operator and function. Use **Getting started** for a full walkthrough, or search below.

overview.title: What is this calculator?
overview.body:
A calculator is a **configuration** (`CalculatorConfig`): input fields, constants, optional macros, intermediate **calculations**, and final **outputs**. Each calc/output has one **formula** stored as a tree (AST). The builder lets you edit that tree as **blocks** or as **text** — both views read and write the **same** tree, so you never maintain two separate formulas.

On the public screen the user fills quantities and properties; the app walks the dependency graph and evaluates every formula in order.

configParts.title: Parts of the configuration
configParts.body:
| Part | User sees it? | Role |
|------|----------------|------|
| **Input** (`field_*`) | Yes — quantity + properties | Values the user types (qty, cost, price, table rows) |
| **Constant** (`const_*`) | No | Fixed numbers you embed in formulas (markup, tax rate) |
| **Macro** (`macro_*`) | No | Reusable formula fragment; drag into any formula like a variable |
| **Calculation** (`calc_*`) | No (intermediate) | Hidden step used by other formulas |
| **Output** (`output_*`) | Yes — after **Calculate** | Final result shown to the user |

**Auto calculations** (badge «Auto») are created when you enable «quantity × property» on an input variable. They appear in a read-only script tab and in the block palette as calc references.

oneFormula.title: One formula, three views
oneFormula.body:
```
CalculatorConfig.expression (JSON AST)  ← only source of truth in the database
        ↑ parse (registry)     ↓ format (registry)
   formula code text          block workspace UI
```

- **Blocks** — Scratch-style workspace: operands, operators, `SUM(…)`, `IF(…)`, groups `( )`.
- **Code** — same language inside `formula { … }` or in the full script sheet.
- **Preview** («Reads as» / breakdown on the calculator page) — human-readable text generated from the AST.

When you add a new operator in the platform, it is implemented once in `lib/formula/nodes/primitives/*.node.ts` and appears in blocks, code, autocomplete, and this help page automatically.

blocksHowTo.title: Block editor — step by step
blocksHowTo.body:
1. Open a **calculation** or **output** field and expand **Calculation logic**.
2. Choose view **Blocks** or **Code + blocks**.
3. Tap an empty **＋** slot (or drag from the palette). The dashed area is the formula workspace.
4. **Palette → Blocks**: fields (qty, properties), constants, macros, other calcs/outputs.
5. **Palette → Actions**: `+ − × ÷`, comparisons, `( )`, `SUM`, `IF`, `ROUND`, row aggregates.
6. Drag **⠿** on a block to move it; drop on another slot to nest inside `SUM` / `IF` / groups.
7. **Reads as** under the workspace shows the formula as text (always synced with blocks).

**IF** and **ROUND** use colored brackets with labeled slots (condition / then / else, value / decimals). **SUM** accepts comma-separated arguments inside one bracket.

codeHowTo.title: Formula code — step by step
codeHowTo.body:
1. In the same panel, switch to **Code** or **Code + blocks**.
2. Write an expression or a small program:

```calc
formula {
  local subtotal = field_item.qty * field_item.var_cost
  return ROUND(subtotal * const_markup, 2)
}
```

3. **Locals** must appear before `return`. Names are lowercase identifiers.
4. References: `field_id.qty`, `field_id.var_cost`, `const_id`, `calc_id`, `output_id`, `macro_id`.
5. Comparisons return **1** (true) or **0** (false). `IF(condition, then, else)` treats any non-zero condition as true.
6. Invalid syntax is **not** saved to blocks until the parser accepts it (debounced while typing).
7. Use **Ctrl/Cmd+S** in the code sheet to apply the whole project; in a single formula field, changes apply when you save the calculator.

Autocomplete (Ctrl+Space) lists fields, functions, and script keywords.

unifiedSync.title: Keeping blocks and code in sync
unifiedSync.body:
- Editing **blocks** updates the code panel immediately (format from registry).
- Editing **code** updates blocks after a short pause once the text parses.
- Opening **Code** (toolbar) opens the **full calculator script** split into tabs (`inputs.calc`, `constants.calc`, …). **Apply** merges all tabs into the same `CalculatorConfig` the block UI uses.
- If you change the builder while the script sheet is open and you have **not** edited the script, the sheet reloads from the builder automatically.
- If you **have** edited the script, a banner offers **Reload from builder** so you do not accidentally overwrite your text.

There is still only one JSON config — the sheet is a text projection, not a second database.

fullScript.title: Full script (Code sheet)
fullScript.body:
The **Code** button in the builder toolbar opens all declarations at once:

| Tab | Content |
|-----|--------|
| `inputs.calc` | `input field_… { … }` |
| `constants.calc` | `constant const_… { … }` |
| `macros.calc` | `macro macro_… { formula { … } }` |
| `calculations.calc` | `calc calc_… { formula { … } }` |
| `outputs.calc` | `output output_… { formula { … } }` |
| `auto-calculations.calc` | read-only auto totals |

Directives: `#include "file.calc"`, `#use "template-id"` (preset). See the **Calculator script** tab below for syntax cards.

Repo reference: `docs/calculator-script.md`.

evaluation.title: How values are computed
evaluation.body:
1. Collect user **quantities** and **line-item rows**.
2. Run **auto calcs** and user **calculations** in dependency order (`field-graph` detects cycles).
3. Evaluate each formula via **registry** (`evaluateExpressionViaRegistry`).
4. Run **outputs** last.
5. **Locals** inside one output are evaluated inside that field only.

Division by zero returns **0** with a warning in logs. `ROUND(x, n)` clamps `n` to 0–10.

tips.title: Tips for beginners
tips.body:
- Start from a **preset** (typography, salon, print shop) in the builder, then tweak blocks.
- Use **calc** fields for long intermediate steps; keep **outputs** short.
- Use **macros** when the same sub-expression appears in several formulas.
- For tables (line items), use `SUM_ROWS(table_id, row.qty * row.var_cost)` in code or **SUM rows** in blocks.
- **?** on palette blocks and **Help** in the header open this page.
- Run tests after script changes: `npx vitest run tests/formula`.
